items.followUp: Define work and describe three forms of energy.

rubric.why: This states the textbook definition of energy.
rubric.description: Defines energy as the capacity to do work.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is a form of energy associated with motion.
rubric.description: Identifies kinetic energy and links it to motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct form and explanation.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with position or configuration.
rubric.description: Identifies potential energy and links it to position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct form and explanation.

rubric.why: A third form with a correct description completes the note on three forms.
rubric.description: Describes heat (thermal) energy as a form of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heat/thermal energy and describing its relation to particles or heat transfer.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.
Heat energy is associated with the random motion of particles and is transferred from a hotter body to a colder body.

items.followUp: Write the symbols of four SI base units other than metre and kilogram.

rubric.why: These are two correctly named SI base units with their symbols.
rubric.description: Gives metre and kilogram with correct symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct unit-symbol pairs.

rubric.why: These are two more correctly named SI base units with their symbols.
rubric.description: Gives second and ampere with correct symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct unit-symbol pairs.

modelAnswer: Metre (m)
Kilogram (kg)
Second (s)
Ampere (A)

items.followUp: Why is a screw gauge suitable for measuring the diameter of a thin sheet?

rubric.why: A wire has a very small diameter, so it is difficult to measure with an ordinary ruler.
rubric.description: States that a wire's diameter is very small.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the small size being measured.

rubric.why: A screw gauge has a small least count and gives a more precise measurement of small dimensions.
rubric.description: Explains the screw gauge's precision or small least count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking its precision/small least count to accurate measurement.

modelAnswer: The diameter of a wire is very small and is difficult to measure accurately with an ordinary ruler.
A screw gauge has a small least count, so it can measure the wire's diameter more precisely.

items.followUp: State Newton's first law of motion and explain what happens when the resultant force on a body is zero.

rubric.why: The law concerns bodies at rest or moving uniformly in a straight line.
rubric.description: Identifies the states of motion covered by the law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating rest and uniform straight-line motion.

rubric.why: The law applies when no resultant external force acts on the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying zero net/resultant force.

modelAnswer: Newton's first law deals with bodies at rest and bodies moving with uniform velocity in a straight line.
It states that a body remains at rest or continues this uniform motion unless acted upon by a non-zero resultant external force.

items.followUp: State Newton's second law of motion and write its mathematical form for a body of constant mass.

rubric.why: This gives the law's central relationship between force and change in momentum.
rubric.description: States that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportionality statement.

rubric.why: The change in momentum is in the force's direction; for constant mass this gives F = ma.
rubric.description: Gives the direction and/or the constant-mass relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction statement or F = ma.

modelAnswer: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
For constant mass, this relation is written as F = ma.

items.followUp: Why is the gravitational force between two small objects difficult to detect?

rubric.why: Ordinary nearby objects have relatively small masses.
rubric.description: Identifies the small masses of ordinary bodies as a reason.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating ordinary bodies' small masses to weak attraction.

rubric.why: Their mutual gravitational attraction is too small to notice compared with everyday forces; Earth's large mass makes its gravitational effect noticeable.
rubric.description: States that the attraction is negligible or contrasts it with Earth's large mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining why the force is not normally perceived.

modelAnswer: The gravitational force between ordinary objects around us is extremely small because their masses are small.
This force is negligible compared with everyday forces, whereas the Earth's very large mass produces a noticeable gravitational force.

items.followUp: Explain why a passenger standing in a moving bus tends to fall backward when the bus starts suddenly.

rubric.why: The passenger's body tends to maintain its initial state of motion due to inertia.
The feet move with the bus while the upper body tends to remain in its previous state, making the passenger fall forward when braking.
rubric.description: Explains the different motion of the bus/lower body and upper body during sudden braking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing this forward-fall mechanism.

modelAnswer: When the bus brakes suddenly, the passenger's feet and lower body stop with the bus.
The upper body tends to continue moving forward due to inertia of motion, so the passenger falls forward.

items.followUp: Define gravitational acceleration and state its sign when downward is taken as positive and when upward is taken as positive.

rubric.why: This defines g as the acceleration caused by gravity, especially for a freely falling body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as acceleration due to gravity.

rubric.why: The sign of g depends on the chosen positive direction; gravity acts downward.
rubric.description: Gives the signs of g for the stated direction conventions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct signs.

modelAnswer: Gravitational acceleration (g) is the acceleration produced in a freely falling body by the gravitational force of the Earth.
If downward is taken as the positive direction, g is positive.
If upward is taken as the positive direction, g is negative.
